featureRef: 12.16 Setting and changing an employee's salary
name: Record what an employee is paid, approve it before it takes effect, and keep every previous figure
priorityReason: Payroll has no figure to calculate from until this exists, and a salary changed without record cannot be defended.

goal.capability: to record what an employee is paid and have it approved before it takes effect
goal.outcome: payroll calculates from an agreed figure, and every change to it can be traced to a date and an approver

secondaryActors.involvement: Sets the salary budget for a role when the vacancy is listed, and uses the agreed salary in payroll.
Approves the salary and any change to it, where the Super Admin has configured that approval.

Is paid on it and sees only their own.

preconditions.condition: An active staff record exists for the employee.

An authenticated session exists. Who may set and who approves is configuration, set by the Super Admin (BR-4).

postConditions: The employee's agreed salary and pay basis are recorded in the salary section of their record — the monthly amount and the daily rate derived from it.
It was approved before it took effect, by whichever role the Super Admin configured.
The figure was recorded against the salary budget set for that role when the vacancy was listed.
A change carries the date it takes effect, the previous figure, the new figure and who approved it, and the previous figure is kept as history.
Payroll calculates from the figure in force for the month being run, not from the latest figure.
The salary and its history are visible only to the roles the visibility rule names.
No salary took effect unapproved, and no previous figure was overwritten.

dataFields.name: Role salary budget
dataFields.validation: The amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay for the role. Set by Accounts when the vacancy is listed (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Monthly amount
dataFields.validation: The agreed monthly salary. Greater than zero, and recorded against the budget for that role (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Daily rate
dataFields.validation: Derived from the monthly amount, not typed. Payroll uses it to value a day (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Effective from
dataFields.validation: The date the figure takes effect. Payroll reads the figure in force for the month being run (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Previous amount
dataFields.validation: The figure this replaces, kept as history (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Change reason
dataFields.validation: 20 to 500 characters. Required for a change to an approved salary.
dataFields.example: Annual increment of 8% approved by the board for the 2026-27 session.
dataFields.requiredWhen: An approved salary is being changed

dataFields.name: Return reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required to return a salary unapproved.
dataFields.example: This exceeds the budget set for the role. Take it to the board first.

dataFields.name: Approved by
dataFields.validation: Whichever role the Super Admin configured, the Principal by default (BR-4).

businessRules.rule: When a vacancy is listed, Accounts set the salary budget for that role — the amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay for it. It is the figure the agreed salary is later recorded against.

When the staff record is created, the agreed salary and the pay basis are recorded in the salary section against the budget set for that role. A figure agreed with no reference to a budget is a figure nobody planned for.
The pay basis is the monthly amount and the daily rate derived from it. The daily rate is derived rather than typed, so the two can never disagree.
The salary is approved before it takes effect. Who sets it and who approves it is configuration set by the Super Admin; by default the School Admin sets it and the Principal approves it.
A salary awaiting approval is not in force. Payroll finds no figure and does not pay on a proposal.
A change is recorded with the date it takes effect, the previous figure, the new figure and who approved it. The previous figure is kept as history and is never overwritten.
Payroll always calculates from the figure in force for the month being run, not from the latest figure. A rise effective in August does not change what July was paid.
The salary and its history are visible only to the roles the visibility rule names.
An effective date may be in the future, so a rise agreed in June and effective in August is recorded once and takes effect by itself.
Two figures for the same employee may not have overlapping effective periods. A new figure's effective date closes the previous one.

The visibility rule says the School Admin cannot see any salary, while this feature makes the School Admin the one who sets it. The two cannot both hold, and this use case cannot be built correctly until the school decides which gives way.
A salary is never deleted. An employee who leaves keeps their salary history, because payroll and tax records reference it.

transitions.condition: Submitted with an amount and an effective date.
Approved and the effective date has arrived (BR-4, BR-5).
Returned with a reason. Nothing is in force.
A later figure is approved and its effective date arrives (BR-10).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → HR → Recruitment → Role salary budget
basicFlow.userAction: Sets the salary budget for the role when the vacancy is listed — the amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the budget the agreed figure will later be measured against.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → HR → Staff record → Salary section → Set salary
basicFlow.userAction: Records the agreed salary and the pay basis against the budget set for that role.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Derives the daily rate from the monthly amount and shows the figure against the role's budget.
Routes it to whichever role the Super Admin configured, the Principal by default. Nothing is in force meanwhile.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the figure against the budget and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Puts it in force from its effective date, and closes the previous figure's period.

basicFlow.userAction: Changes the salary later, giving the date it takes effect and a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Keeps the previous figure as history and routes the change through the same approval.
Gives payroll the figure in force for the month being run, not the latest figure.
Shows the salary and its history only to the roles the visibility rule names.

alternateFlows.condition: The agreed figure exceeds the budget set for the role
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded and flagged against the budget rather than blocked, and the approver sees the excess before deciding (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept the figure
alternateFlows.navigation: Salary approvals → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns with a reason and nothing is in force. Payroll finds no figure and does not pay on a proposal (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: A rise is agreed in June to take effect in August
alternateFlows.navigation: Salary section → Change salary → Effective from
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded once with a future effective date and takes effect by itself. July is still paid at the old figure (BR-7, BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: Payroll is run for a month before a rise took effect
alternateFlows.behaviour: The figure in force for that month is used, not the latest one (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The Super Admin has configured a different setter
alternateFlows.behaviour: Whichever role is configured sets the salary. This is where the contradiction with the visibility rule is resolved, by moving the setting to a role that can already see it (BR-4, BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: A role without the right opens the salary section
alternateFlows.behaviour: The section is not returned at all, per the visibility rule (BR-8).

exceptions.condition: The monthly amount is zero or less
exceptions.messageShown: Enter an amount greater than zero.

exceptions.condition: No budget was set for the role
exceptions.systemResponse: The figure cannot be recorded against one (BR-2).
exceptions.messageShown: No salary budget is set for this role. Ask Accounts to set it.

exceptions.condition: The setter attempts to approve their own salary submission
exceptions.messageShown: Only the configured approver can approve a salary.

exceptions.condition: Payroll is run while the salary is awaiting approval
exceptions.systemResponse: No figure is in force and the employee is not paid on a proposal (BR-5).
exceptions.messageShown: This employee has no approved salary. Payroll cannot calculate for them.

exceptions.condition: A change is submitted with no reason
exceptions.messageShown: Give a reason for the change.

exceptions.condition: The new effective date overlaps a figure already in force
exceptions.messageShown: A salary is already in force from 01-08-2026. Set a later effective date.

exceptions.condition: The effective date is before the employee's joining date
exceptions.messageShown: The effective date cannot be before the joining date.

exceptions.condition: An attempt is made to overwrite a previous figure
exceptions.messageShown: A previous salary is kept as history. Record a new figure with its effective date.
A salary is never deleted. Payroll and tax records reference it.

exceptions.condition: The acting role cannot see the salary section but is configured to set it
exceptions.systemResponse: The contradiction surfaces here and the action cannot proceed (BR-11).
exceptions.messageShown: This role cannot see the salary section and so cannot set a salary. The visibility configuration needs correcting.

sideEffects.effect: Payroll calculates the month's pay from the figure in force.
The salary section written here is governed by the visibility rule.
The figure is recorded against the budget set when the vacancy was listed.
The salary attaches to the staff record without appearing on the general record.

departures.requirement: A previous salary figure is never overwritten or deleted. Every figure an employee has been paid on stays readable with its effective period.
Payroll resolves the figure in force for the month being run. A later rise never changes what an earlier month was paid.
The daily rate is derived from the monthly amount at every use, never stored as a separate typed figure that could drift.
Until the school decides whether the School Admin may see a salary, this use case cannot be built correctly. The setter must be a role that can see the section.
Salaries and their history are retained 7 years after exit, since payroll and tax records reference them.

openQuestions.question: The visibility rule says the School Admin cannot see any salary, while this feature makes the School Admin the one who sets it. The document states the two cannot both hold. Either the School Admin is given sight of the salary section, or the setting of salary moves to a role that can already see it.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved, and it blocks this use case and the visibility one together.

openQuestions.question: Is the daily rate derived by dividing the monthly amount by the calendar days, the working days, or a fixed figure?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the three give materially different deductions.

openQuestions.question: May a salary be agreed above the role's budget, and who authorises that?
openQuestions.assumption: Flagged to the approver as modelled, not blocked. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Can a salary be backdated to a month payroll has already run, and what happens to the difference?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it would need a payroll adjustment.

openQuestions.question: Is the salary a single figure, or does it break into components such as basic, allowances and deductions?
openQuestions.assumption: A single monthly figure as modelled. Most payrolls need components.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
